channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's CEC Head Reports to President Tokayev on Maslikhat Election Preparations
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission, Nurlan Abdirov, briefed President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on preparations for the upcoming maslikhat elections on November 29, 2026. The President emphasized the importance of fair elections and equal conditions for all participants. Early termination of maslikhats' powers was announced on September 24.

item.title: 49-Year-Old Man Shot Dead in Aktobe; Suspect Sought by Police
item.description: The body of a 49-year-old man, who died from a gunshot wound, was found in Aktobe. Social media reports suggest an unknown assailant broke into a private residence, stealing the victim's money and car. Police have launched a criminal investigation and are actively searching for the suspect.

item.title: Kazakh Scientists Present Findings on Kok-Zhailau Resort Environmental Impact
item.description: Kazakh scientists have presented comprehensive research results concerning the proposed Almaty SuperSki mountain resort at Kok-Zhailau. The studies address the potential environmental consequences, including impacts on biodiversity, water resources, and geological stability. These findings are intended to inform ongoing public discussions about the project's feasibility and ecological risks.

item.title: Two Underground Call Centers Handling Crypto Transactions Busted in Tashkent
item.description: Tashkent police uncovered two clandestine call centers suspected of illegally handling cryptocurrency transactions totaling $576,000. Individuals were arrested for allegedly facilitating payments for offshore online casinos and illegal betting, which the Interior Ministry described as money laundering. Seized items include cash, laptops, phones, and Starlink devices.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Telegram Bot for Tax System Reform Proposals
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a Telegram bot, "Tax Proposals" (@soliqtaklif_bot), allowing citizens and entrepreneurs to submit suggestions for reforming the tax system. The initiative aims to gather ideas for simplifying tax reporting, improving electronic services, and reducing bureaucracy. Useful proposals may be considered for future legislation.

item.title: Tashkent Authorities Investigate Possible Animal Poisoning in Chilanzar District
item.description: Tashkent's Uchtepa district administration is investigating reports of mass deaths of stray animals and birds in the Chilanzar district. Social media posts suggest poisoning as a possible cause. Authorities have involved specialized services and law enforcement to determine the cause and ensure public safety.

item.title: Almaty Office Sales Soar 83% in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Office property sales in Almaty surged by 83.2% to 75.4 billion tenge in January-September 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Investors are driving demand, with average sale prices increasing by 56% year-on-year to 1.25 million tenge per square meter.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan Elevate Economic Cooperation to New Level
item.description: A business forum on the economic potential and investment opportunities of Tashkent region was held in Tokyo. Over 200 Japanese companies participated, fostering dialogue and showcasing investment projects. Uzbekistan's ambassador and the Tashkent region governor highlighted the growing strategic partnership, with over 170 Japanese companies currently operating in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Culture Ministry Proposes Media Headquarters for Emergency Situations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Culture is proposing the creation of an operational media headquarters to coordinate public communication during emergencies. This temporary interdepartmental mechanism aims to provide citizens with consistent and verified information, updating the current emergency information system from 2015. The ministry will decide on convening the headquarters in coordination with the Presidential Administration's Information Policy Service.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Hold Two Presidential Election Voting Opportunities for Citizens
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will offer citizens two opportunities to participate in presidential elections. A trial vote will be held on November 18, 2026, with 2,492 polling stations open nationwide for voters to check their data and familiarize themselves with the biometric identification and voting process. The official presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Discusses Preparations for Early Maslikhat Elections
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the Central Election Commission chairman to discuss preparations for the early elections of maslikhat deputies at all levels, scheduled for November 29, 2026. The President emphasized the need for elections based on the constitutional principle of 'Law and Order' and equal conditions for candidates.

item.title: Taliban Deputy Prime Minister Claims Significant Advances in Drone Production
item.description: Abdul Salam Hanafi, the administrative deputy of the Taliban prime minister, stated that the group is equipped with "the most modern" weapons and has made significant progress in drone technology. He asserted that Afghan forces can now suppress any enemy threats. The Taliban previously displayed some rudimentary suicide drones.

item.title: Pakistan Foreign Minister Urges Afghanistan to Address Neighboring Countries' Security Concerns
item.description: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar called for a peaceful and stable Afghanistan. He urged Afghan authorities to address the security concerns of neighboring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism, during the ECO Council of Ministers meeting in Islamabad. Dar stated that a secure environment is essential for regional economic partnerships.

item.title: Tokayev Orders Equal Conditions for Candidates in Upcoming Mazhilis Elections
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed to ensure equal conditions for all candidates and political parties in the upcoming elections for maslikhats. He emphasized the importance of holding elections based on the constitutional principle of "Law and Order" to strengthen local representative bodies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Imposes Six-Month Ban on White Sugar Imports
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has temporarily banned the import of white sugar from third countries and EAEU states for six months. The restriction, effective in 10 days, excludes certain sugar types and transit shipments. The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Economy will monitor domestic supply and prices, proposing adjustments if shortages arise.

item.title: Kyrgyz National Bank Denies Rumors of Global Banking System Failures
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has refuted rumors circulating on social media about potential global internet, communication, and banking system failures. The bank assures that all commercial banks are operating stably and providing full services. It advises verifying information through official channels and contacting banks directly for inquiries.

item.title: Taliban Justice Minister Claims Man-Made Laws Contradict Islamic Sharia
item.description: Abdul Hakim Shara’i, the Taliban’s Minister of Justice, asserted that the Quran is the group's constitution and that their laws are derived from Islamic Sharia. He claimed man-made laws are contrary to Islam. Afghanistan currently lacks a legitimate governance system, having repealed its previous constitution and other laws. The Taliban has banned political parties and suppressed dissent.

item.title: Tajikistan Bans Sale, Gifting, and Inheritance of Awarded Firearms
item.description: Tajikistan has prohibited the sale, gifting, and inheritance of awarded short-barreled rifled firearms and their ammunition. This restriction is stipulated in amendments to the Law on Weapons, signed by President Emomali Rahmon. Awarded weapons are defined as those received via presidential decree, government resolution, or foreign state awards. Holders cannot sell, gift, or bequeath these specific firearms.

item.title: World Bank Recommends Phasing Out Kazakhstan's '7-20-25' Mortgage Program
item.description: World Bank experts have advised Kazakhstan to gradually phase out its preferential '7-20-25' mortgage program and transition to market-based lending. The bank suggests moving away from a state-dominated model with large subsidies towards a balanced housing finance system. The report questions the program's effectiveness and alignment with the National Bank's mandate.

item.title: Over 100 Kyrgyz Citizens Stranded in Tashkent En Route to Umrah Pilgrimage
item.description: More than 100 Kyrgyz citizens, en route to the Umrah pilgrimage, have been stranded in Tashkent since November 12. A travel company representative allegedly promised flights but has not provided tickets, demanding additional payment. Some elderly pilgrims are experiencing health issues. Authorities are urged to intervene.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes New Law to Hold Banks Accountable for Fraudulent Loans
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a new bill to enhance citizen protection against financial fraud. Banks would be required to suspend suspicious loan disbursements and allow victims to seek asset freezes before filing lawsuits. The draft legislation aims to amend several key legal codes and laws related to banking and consumer credit.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Issue Tokenized Government Bonds in Early 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch government bonds as digital tokens in Q1 2027, enabling digital recording and transfer of ownership. The National Bank governor announced the initiative, developed with the Ministry of Finance. The central bank has already tested tokenized notes, with plans to integrate KASE, AIFC, and Alatau City for promotion.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Platform to Connect Investors with Local Producers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agency for Industrial Cooperation and State Procurement has launched a new platform, demo.icppa.uz, to facilitate connections between investors and local manufacturers. The resource aims to consolidate data on major investment projects, material needs, and available products, featuring a product catalog and a unified producer registry.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Bill Proposes Government Checks for Children's Online Games and Apps
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing a bill that mandates government checks for online games and apps before children can access them, and restricts minors' online shopping. The legislation requires platforms to label potentially risky features and offer parental controls. Unverified content may be blocked, and platforms could face liability for violations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Administrative Reform to Strengthen Regions and Reduce Migration
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is contemplating an administrative reform aimed at consolidating and strengthening its regions. The proposed reform seeks to create more flexible and economically robust regions, thereby reducing internal migration pressures on the capital. The current multi-tiered system is seen as inefficient and fragmented.

item.title: Taliban detain four Shia clerics in Bamyan
item.description: Sources in Bamyan confirmed that Taliban intelligence arrested and imprisoned four Shia clerics. The clerics were members of the oversight board for Shia seminaries in Bamyan and were arrested while distributing tuition fees for religious schools. The Taliban also confiscated the tuition fee transfer documents.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Five-Year Prison for Bloggers Promoting Financial Pyramids
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering stricter penalties for creating and advertising financial pyramids, including up to five years imprisonment for bloggers. The proposed legislation also allows for temporary blocking of suspicious bank accounts and crypto-assets without a court order. The changes aim to combat financial fraud.

item.title: Uzbekistan Blocks Nearly 2.1 Million Attempts to Access Phishing Websites
item.description: From January to September 2026, Uzbekistan blocked almost 2.1 million attempts to access phishing sites. The number of such attempts in Q3 2026 was more than triple that of Q1 2025. Common scams involve emails mimicking employers or services, with 13% of employees clicking on fake password expiry links in company tests.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airport Explores UNODC Partnership for Central Asian Logistics Hub
item.description: The director of Navoi International Airport met with UNODC representatives to discuss the airport's strategic location and logistics potential. The focus was on strengthening its role as a key transport and logistics center in Central Asia, including improving supply chains for strategic raw materials and ensuring transport security.

item.title: Uzbekistan's First Nuclear Plant to Use Dry Cooling to Conserve Water Resources
item.description: Uzbekistan's first nuclear power plant, under construction in Jizzakh, will utilize a dry cooling system to minimize water consumption. This decision addresses concerns over the country's limited water supplies, with the system using air to dissipate heat instead of water. The technology's effectiveness in hot weather requires further attention.

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces Power Outages Despite Increased Generation Capacity Due to Network Issues
item.description: Despite a 50% increase in power generation capacity over five years, Uzbekistan continues to experience electricity disruptions. The Central Bank attributes this to aging networks, energy losses, and insufficient infrastructure capacity. The World Bank is providing $100 million for substation modernization and digitalization.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Caution on Loans for Housing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov advised citizens against taking bank loans for home construction or renovation, especially at high interest rates. He emphasized calculating repayment ability and warned that even profitable businesses might not cover loan costs. The president stressed financial literacy and responsible borrowing.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Exports Outpace Imports in January-September, Driven by Strong Trade Growth
item.description: Kazakhstan's foreign trade turnover reached $116.8 billion in January-September 2026, an 11.8% increase year-on-year. Exports grew by 18.1% to $68.4 billion, while imports rose 4% to $48.4 billion. China and Russia remain the largest trading partners. Key exports include crude oil, refined copper, and radioactive elements.

item.title: Nurbank Repays Additional 6.5 Billion Tenge of State Support Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Nurbank has prematurely repaid another 6.5 billion tenge of state support, bringing the total early repayment to 11 billion tenge. The bank received state support in 2020 through subordinated bonds. This early repayment strengthens the bank's financial stability and fulfills its obligations to the state ahead of schedule.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Tobol River Site for Third Nuclear Power Plant
item.description: Kazakhstan is evaluating a site near the Tobol River in the northern Kostanay region for its third nuclear power plant. This location is being considered alongside two other potential sites in the east and west. The Tobol River could provide sufficient water for reactor cooling, according to the chairman of Kazakhstan's Atomic Energy Agency.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports Over $23 Million Lost to Fraud in Nine Months
item.description: Uzbekistan has registered tens of thousands of fraud cases involving bank cards and e-wallets, resulting in total losses exceeding 278 billion soums (approximately $23 million) from January to October 2026. The Central Bank reported that malicious apps, Telegram hacks, and online scams were common methods used by fraudsters.

item.title: Bishkek Coal Reserves Reach 16,000 Tons, Prices Vary by District
item.description: Coal reserves in Bishkek have increased to approximately 16,000 tons across four districts. The price for 'Kara-Keche' coal starts at 7,000 soms per ton, according to the city administration. Various coal types are available at different prices, with city services monitoring availability and prices.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allows Civil Servants to Take on Additional Paid Work
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree permitting civil and municipal employees in political and special positions to engage in additional paid activities. This allows for income from educational, expert, scientific, and creative work related to their professional field, provided they obtain consent from their appointing authority and avoid conflicts of interest. They can also participate in public benefit activities for NGOs in healthcare, education, charity, and volunteerism.

item.title: Kazakhstan Drafts First Law Partially Written by Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing its first legislative act partially drafted by an AI model named AI-Quryltai. The draft law, focused on 'The Digital and Information Security of Children,' incorporates over 120 amendments generated by the AI, which was trained on extensive regulatory documents. These amendments include provisions for mandatory parental controls and age-restriction filtering for digital entertainment. All AI-generated content has undergone manual review by parliament members and experts.

item.title: Taliban Interior Minister Urges Leaders to Avoid Public Discontent
item.description: Sartaj Haqqani, the Taliban's Interior Minister, has called on group leaders and members to avoid actions that would cause public hatred. He emphasized that the group's system is for serving the people, not imposing rule, and that distancing from the public will increase animosity. Haqqani also stressed the importance of explaining the Islamic system's goals to the public at a grassroots level.
